evidence: The LC records are distinct people: n50044336 is Anthony Arthur Long (born 1937), author of The Hellenistic Philosophers; n78085939 is Austin Long (1936–2010), the geochemist and Radiocarbon editor. Moreover, b mixes that scientist’s Radiocarbon After Four Decades (1992) with the nuclear-policy specialist Austin Long’s Managing U.S. Nuclear Operations (2022). Neither is the classical philosopher.

The initials-only a combines M. G. Smith’s Hausa social-status work, M. S. Smith’s Greek Precedents for Claudius, and Monica L. Smith’s Networks, Territories, and the Cartography of Ancient States (2005). It is not a coherent Martin Ferguson Smith bibliography; b’s books concern Diogenes of Oinoanda’s Epicurean inscription.

The LC records describe different people: n80057203 is Edmund Kerchever Chambers (1866–1954), the Shakespeare and medieval-stage scholar; n82163778 is Erve Chambers (born 1942), Maryland anthropologist, Oregon PhD 1973. The Elizabethan Stage and William Shakespeare belong to the former career; Applied Anthropology, Tourism and Culture, and Native Tours belong to the latter.

LC n50027502 identifies James Dixon Douglas (born 1922) through The New Bible Dictionary (1962). LC n50027499 identifies Jack D. Douglas (born 1937) through The Social Meanings of Suicide (1967). These are distinct authority records for the Christian reference editor and the sociologist of suicide, deviance, and everyday life, respectively.

The publisher credits Vitruvius and Greek Aqueducts (1999) to Michael Lewis, so a’s Mark anchor does not identify its cited author. The Bioarchaeology of Children (2007) is by Mary E. Lewis. The aqueduct article and the child-skeleton/palaeopathology books belong to different authors.
